podcast.body: A major hit that reached number 11 on the pop chart and number 1 on the R&B chart. It was co-written by Bo Diddley (lyrics, credited to Ethel Smith) and Jody Williams (music), with Mickey and Sylvia credited as arrangers, presumably for their changes including the famous spoken word section. Bo Diddley later sold his share to Sylvia. The song became a classic, covered by many artists. "Lovey's Strange was a big hit. It went to number 11 in the pop chart, and number 1 on the R&B chart."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 49: "Love is Strange" by Mickey and Sylvia

podcast.body: Carole King and Gerry Goffin worked on a song in the style of "Love Is Strange" for Mickey & Sylvia, at a time when Atlantic Records was looking for new material for the duo. "King mentioned that she knew that Atlantic were looking for a new song for Mickey and Sylvia, and the two of them worked on a song based on the style of Love Is Strange, which they completed very quickly and talked to Atlantic."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 89: "Will You Love Me Tomorrow?" by the Shirelles

podcast.body: This song was performed by the duo Mickey and Sylvia, which included Sylvia Robinson, who would later go on to found Sugar Hill Records and produce "Rapper's Delight." The song gained renewed popular recognition from its inclusion in the movie "Dirty Dancing," where Baby and Johnny dance to it. "if you remember that scene in dirty dancing when Baby and Johnny were dancing to love his strange, she was that Sylvia."
